action: Place the probe in a transverse orientation. Ensure the probe indicator points to the patient's right.
interpretation: Establish the standard transverse scanning plane.

action: Apply gentle pressure. Slide the transducer towards the patient's right.
interpretation: Scan laterally to locate the colon. Identify the characteristic 'dirty shadowing' artifact produced by bowel gas in the colon.

action: Focus attention on the superficial near field.
interpretation: Visualize the abdominal wall musculature located above the deeper structures.

action: Slide the transducer inferiorly towards the patient's feet.
interpretation: Follow the dirty shadowing until it ends. Identify this termination point as the level of the cecum.

action: Slide the probe superiorly back up into the abdomen. Perform exploratory micro-movements.
interpretation: Search the area to identify the structure most consistent with the appendix.

action: Locate the attachment to the cecum. Optimize the image to resolve fine details.
interpretation: Identify a 'small, blind-ended structure' attached to the cecum. Note that the structure measures only a couple of millimeters in thickness, confirming it is a normal, healthy appendix.
